## 2026-11-17 02:29 · The reviewer to the lead (SR Leagues review 2.200 (code): overtime on the result)

REVIEW of step 2.200 "Overtime on the result", lane/2.200-overtime at c1597fe. This is the independent code review. I changed nothing and `git status` is clean.

FINDINGS

1. Medium. apps/web/src/features/schedule-pages/live-game-list.tsx:40-56 with build-schedule.ts:159. A schedule, home, team or standings page that was open while the game was live keeps saying "Final" with no OT after the game ends in overtime, and it stays that way until the person reloads. The game's own page does show "Final, OT", because `redrawsFor` redraws it from the server. So a fan watching the home page during a game won in OT never sees the mark, and the spec says the mark is shown "everywhere its result is shown". Proof from the code: `applyUpdate` only keeps a `finalText` that `gameView` wrote when the page was drawn, and it writes one only for a game already final. The league channel (packages/contracts/src/live-channels.ts:60-66) carries `period` but not the regulation `periods`. Tests: schedule-pages.test.ts:433-455 covers only a page drawn after the end, and tests/browser/overtime-test.mjs opens every page after the end. Smallest right fix, with no contract change: give `GameView` the game's regulation periods from the server read (its own format, else the season's), keep `m.period` in `Update`, and in `applyUpdate` give any update to final the mark max(0, period − regulation). Add a unit test: drawn live, then final with period 3 in a halves game, reads "Final, OT". Do not add `periods` to `LeagueScoreMessage`: it is a strictObject, so pages drawn before the release would refuse the new messages. The same fix also makes the "reopened and ended again" card right, which today shows no mark.
2. Low. Release window (T-183's concern). Between migration 0021 and the last old app server stopping, the new app can end a game with a count of 1 or more. If an old server then reopens that game, it writes status live and leaves the count, so `games_overtime_when_final` refuses the reopen. The window is short and the reopen fails cleanly with nothing lost. Fix: a line in the release notes (migrate, then switch every server together). No code.
3. Low, for later languages. `display.finalOvertime_one` is "Final, OT" with no {count}. In a language whose CLDR "one" category covers numbers other than 1 at counts up to 18, it would drop the number; Filipino, for example, puts 2 in "one". English is right. Fix when a catalog is added: a translator's note on the key, or an exact "=1" key.

CHECKED AND SOUND
Migration: each file runs in one transaction (run-migrations.ts), so the drop and re-create of the trigger leave no moment and no failure in which a decided game is unguarded. The new trigger is 0009's, the only definition of it (0011, 0013 and 0016 replaced only the function), plus exactly one line; I compared them with diff. T-183 allows DROP TRIGGER and `npm run check` passes. The two CHECKs pass trivially on existing rows because the new column starts empty. The 18 limit matches the engine (MAX_PERIOD 20, regulation 2 or 4). No path out of final bypasses `update-game-result.ts`: not-started, bin, restore and the published-game edit all act only on games that are not final. `overtimePeriods` is a required field of `GameResultChange`, so every caller has to write it: finish (the End button, a batch from a device back online, the transfer) writes the engine's count; decideGame (typed score, box score, import, forfeit; it acts only on undecided, untracked games), both reopens, cancel, postpone and live writes write null. There is no separate "take back End game"; the scorekeeper's undo is reopen-tracked-game. Regulation comes from `state.rules.periods`, which `withCurrentRules` keeps in step with the game's own fixed format. Reads: one more column on queries that already filter by league, published season and bin; the public schedule is still one query.
Break, fail, put back (all four failed as they should): (a) the new line removed from the trigger: overtime.test "are the result's" failed; with three of 0009's lines removed, game-corrections.test failed three times; (b) regulation hard-coded as 4: six tests failed, halves and quarters both; (c) both reopens keeping the count: five failed, in memory and on the database; (d) a mark shown for 0: three failed. The 78 tests of the lane's files pass, and so do `npm run check` and `npm run typecheck`. I did not run the browser test myself (heavy) and did no design review.
Words: null and 0 draw "Final"; 1 draws "Final, OT" ("final after overtime" for screen readers); 2 draws "Final, 2OT" ("final after 2 overtimes"). A missing plural form falls back to `_other`. Other steps' tests: every change made a check stronger; none weaker or gone.
COLLISIONS: 2.198 (0022, the standings tie rules) does not touch games or the S-7 trigger, so there is no clash in meaning, unless it re-makes that trigger from 0009's text, which would lose this line. 2.196's box-score Total has no overlap: overtime points are already in the score, and box scores keep a null count.

PRODUCT QUESTIONS: none.

May land after a fix round: 1
